We need to propose a retrosynthesis route with at least 5 reactions, using templates in order: ['29646', '1914389', '1914390', '149040', '1914391'].

We must produce JSON route where each reaction node uses the given template_id (as integer? example shows number). Use the given order sequentially from target to precursors.

We need to apply each template to generate precursors. We have applied first three templates partially. Need to get results for each step.

First template 29646 applied to target gave three possible precursors (tuples). The result was a tuple of three strings? Actually result: "(('C/C(=C/[C@H]1O[C@@H](C/C=C/C=C/C(=O)O[Si](C)(C)C(C)(C)C)C[C@H](O)[C@H]1C)CO',), ('C/C(=C/[C@H]1O[C@@H](C/C=C/C=C/C(=O)O)C[C@H](O)[C@H]1C)CO[Si](C)(C)C(C)(C)C',), ('C/C(=C/[C@H]1O[C@@H]([C@@H]1C)/C=C(CO)/C)C',))"

It seems three possible precursors each as a tuple of one SMILES. So we need choose one path that can continue with next template 1914389.

The next template 1914389 applied to the second precursor (with silyl group) succeeded, giving two products: ('C/C(=C/[C@H]1O[C@@H](CC=O)C[C@H](O)[C@H]1C)CO[Si](C)(C)C(C)(C)C', 'CCOC(=O)/C=C/CP(=O)(OCC)OCC').

So the reaction splits target into two fragments: a cyclic part with silyl and a side chain ester? Actually.

Thus after applying 1914389, we have two precursors. Then we need to apply template 1914390 to each? The order says after 1914389, then 1914390. Likely apply 1914390 to one of the precursors (maybe the side chain). We attempted applying 1914390 to the cyclic precursor and got no result. We also tried applying to the side chain (CCOC(=O)/C=C/CP(=O)(OCC)OCC) and got no result.

Maybe we need to apply 1914390 to a different precursor from earlier step. Perhaps we should choose a different precursor from first step that matches 1914389.

First precursor list: 1) C/C(=C/[C@H]1O[C@@H](C/C=C/C=C/C(=O)O[Si](C)(C)C(C)(C)C)C[C@H](O)[C@H]1C)CO (no silyl on acid). 2) C/C(=C/[C@H]1O[C@@H](C/C=C/C=C/C(=O)O)C[C@H](O)[C@H]1C)CO[Si](C)(C)C(C)(C)C (silyl on acid). 3) C/C(=C/[C@H]1O[C@@H]([C@@H]1C)/C=C(CO)/C)C (no side chain). The third is simpler maybe.

We need to apply 1914389 to something; we saw it works on the second (silyl). Maybe we should apply 1914389 to the first (no silyl) maybe also works? Let's test.
